card: This pull request removes avoidable delays and unused setup overhead in several tests and benchmarks. It caps long negative timeouts in p2p and IPC functional tests, respects sanity-mode epochs in a wallet benchmark, and drops unused 100-block chain generation in two wallet unit tests. According to the author, the timeout adjustments alone save approximately eight minutes of accumulated worker time on affected CI jobs. No dependencies are listed.
evidence: PR description: 'The timeout changes alone save approximately eight minutes of accumulated test-worker time on CI jobs running both transports and IPC mining.'

PR description: 'in p2p_node_network_limited replace the expected sync timeout with header/ping barriers and a bounded negative check. At CI timeout factor 40, saves roughly 195 seconds per transport.'
PR description: 'in interface_ipc_mining cap three expected no-event waits at five seconds, saving roughly 105 seconds at factor 40 in CI.'
problem: CI and local test runs spend several minutes waiting on scaled negative timeouts (waiting for events that should not happen) and constructing unused chain state. Developers and CI infrastructure experience slower overall test turnaround times.

risk.why: A mistake in test synchronization or timeouts could cause flaky test failures or false positives in CI.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided, but commits indicate changes touch functional tests, unit test fixtures, and benchmark setup across four files.
summary: Removes unnecessary waits, timeouts, and setup overhead across several functional tests, unit tests, and benchmarks. Specifically, it replaces scaled negative sync timeouts with synchronization barriers in p2p_node_network_limited, caps expected no-event wait durations in interface_ipc_mining, respects the single-epoch setting during benchmark sanity runs for wallet descriptor loading, and switches two wallet unit tests to use BasicTestingSetup instead of mining unused 100-block chains.
uncertainties: The patch diff was not available in the input, so exact implementations and barrier logic could not be directly verified.
